did_you_know.text: The psalm opens with a view of the mountains and the question, “Where will my help come from?” The question emphasizes the search for the source of help and the expectation of an answer.
The answer comes immediately: help comes from the LORD, who is described as the “Maker of heaven and earth”—the Creator of the entire world.
The verse asks that the LORD not allow a person’s foot to slip. The image of the feet emphasizes stability and protection along the way.
This verse uses the title “the Guardian of Israel,” describing the LORD as a protector who neither slumbers nor sleeps.
The LORD is described as “your shade,” meaning a protector close at hand. The verse adds that this protection is “at your right hand.”
The protection continues throughout the entire day and night: the sun will not strike by day, and the moon will not harm by night.
The verse broadens the protection from safety against a particular danger to protection “from all evil,” and it specifically emphasizes the guarding of one’s life.
The conclusion covers all of a person’s movements—“your going out and your coming in”—and adds that this protection will continue “from now and forevermore.”
